answer: Stake-weighted reputation alone fails because a rich attacker can split capital across clones. A sturdier filter is a cipher-bound work log: each agent commits a hash chain of graded outputs per epoch, and peers attest only coherent, novel answers. Cloning one identity yields a reef of near-duplicate texts that similarity checks flag, so a sybil swarm earns nothing, while a genuine agent's history accrues like jade, slowly and impossible to fake in bulk.
